newsitem.title: UAE: Dubai Aluminium opens $503 mln expansion project.
newsitem.headline: Dubai Aluminium opens $503 mln expansion project.

text.p: Dubai Aluminium (Dubal) on Sunday opened its $503 million Falcon expansion project in the heart of a region its chief executive said could become a significant producer of the metal in the next decade.

"The Gulf is rich in natural gas resources. It is natural that smelters be built here because long-term energy supply agreements can be made. This region could be a significant producer of aluminium in the next decade," Ian Rugeroni said.
Power to generate the smelting process is one of the single biggest costs of production.

Rugeroni was speaking to Reuters at a ceremony at which United Arab Emirates Finance and Industry Minister Sheikh Hamdan bin Rashid al-Maktoum inaugurated Dubal's new 240-cell potline, which produces about 350 tonnes of aluminium a day.

"Falcon increases our production by 50 percent to a total capacity of 375,000 tonnes of quality aluminium per year. With this expansion Dubal will truly take its rightful place among the world's top aluminium smelters," Sheikh Hamdan said.
Dubal is one of two Gulf producers. The other, Aluminium Bahrain, has capacity of around half a million tonnes. Oman also plans to set up a 480,000 tonne capacity smelter.
Rugeroni said Dubal, one of the UAE's largest non-oil foreign exchange earners, continued to work against a six percent European Union tariff on aluminium imports.

"The six percent duty is still our major issue. It is a tax that is discriminatory and is difficult to defend. If the region is going to sell, it cannot be shut out of a third of the world's market (Europe)," he said.

"European consumers are being penalised, paying about $100 more a tonne above their competitors in Japan and the United States. A lot of Italian and U.K. (firms) would like to buy from us. We are saying, try our stuff and hopefully the six percent will go. It (Europe) is a natural market for us."

Dubal sales general manager Malcolm McHale, said Dubal's infrastructure was currently capable of supporting capacity of 500,000 tonnes of production a year. "But we must develop parnerships with European companies before expanding again."
He said the most promising future partnerships would focus on sheet ingot production.

Some 80 percent of Dubal's output is currently destined for Asia -- mainly Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Indonesia and the Philippines. About 15 percent is sold in the Middle East and around five percent goes to European customers.
